meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: No general state final-pay statute; wages are due on the regular payday (Georgia requires at least semi-monthly pay, O.C.G.A. 34-7-2)
facts.summary: Georgia has no general final-pay deadline; final wages are due on the regular payday, and most employees must be paid at least semi-monthly.
facts.evidence_quote: I resigned 3 weeks ago. My boss keeps telling me to come back to get my last pay check. Each time I go back he tells me to come back on their next regular pay day. What should I do? Call the U. S. Department of Labor Wage and Hour Division.
facts.notes: Basis: absence of statute. GA DOL refers final-pay questions to U.S. DOL rather than citing a state deadline. Pay frequency: GA DOL Employer Handbook DOL-224 (https://dol.georgia.gov/document/unemployment-tax/employer-handbook/download) says all employees other than officials and department heads 'must be paid on a semi-monthly or more frequent basis' (O.C.G.A. 34-7-2). Federal: https://www.dol.gov/general/topic/wages/lastpaycheck.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Georgia state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $5.15. Employers covered by the federal FLSA must pay at least $7.25.
facts.evidence_quote: Applicable to employers of 6 or more employees Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $5.15 The State law excludes from coverage any employment that is subject to the federal Fair Labor Standards Act when the federal rate is greater than the State rate. Employers subject to the Fair Labor Standards Act must pay the current Federal minimum wage of $7.25 per hour.
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page. The FLSA federal minimum of $7.25 per hour applies to covered employers, so $5.15 applies only to the few employers not covered by the FLSA.

facts.summary: Georgia is not listed with a final 2026 FUTA credit reduction, so the effective FUTA rate is 0.6% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full 5.4% state credit applies).
facts.evidence_quote: State not listed in the Final 2026 FUTA Credit Reductions table.
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: Georgia base new employer UI rate: 2.64%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law. Rate basis: DOL base rate. It may exclude mandatory surcharges, fund-building rates and assessments; check the state agency or total_new_employer_rate where available.
